Balcony Herb Plan
Introduction
Welcome to your balcony herb garden plan. This guide provides practical steps to successfully grow basil and
mint on your balcony. You will find information on setup, watering, harvesting, and a crucial note on keeping
mint contained.
Herbs Overview
Basil
Uses: Basil is a versatile herb commonly used in Italian cuisine, perfect for sauces, salads, and as a
garnish.
Growth: Basil thrives in warm, sunny conditions.
Container: Use a pot at least 12 inches deep to allow root growth.
Mint
Uses: Mint adds freshness to drinks, desserts, and sauces.
Growth: Mint grows rapidly in almost all conditions.
Container: Plant mint in a separate container to prevent it from overgrowing.
Practical Setup Steps
Choose the right containers: Ensure they have good drainage.
Potting mix: Use a high-quality organic potting soil.
Placement: Position your pots where they will get at least 6 hours of sunlight daily.
Watering Instructions
Basil: Water when the soil feels dry to the touch. Avoid waterlogging.
Mint: Keep the soil consistently moist but not soggy.
Harvesting Advice
Basil: Start harvesting when the plant has at least six leaves. Pick the leaves regularly to encourage
growth.
Mint: Harvest sprigs before the mint flowers for the best flavor.
Safety Note
Mint can become invasive. Always keep it in a separate pot to prevent it from overtaking your balcony space.
